title: Introduce precision-aware fast-path gating and safe-mode fallbacks for runtime kernels
author: Noah Kim
release_notes: Added a precision-aware fast-path gating system and a runtime 'safe-mode' that forces deterministic fallback kernels on error/uncertainty; configurable via runtime flags and per-deployment policies. Improvements target correctness under mixed-precision and aggressive kernel selection with minimal perf impact.
description:
Motivation and summary: We observed rare correctness regressions in production when the runtime selected aggressive high-throughput kernels (mixed-precision, fused attention variants) under tail-case sequence patterns. These regressions correlate with two factors: (1) precision toggles (bfloat16/int8 paths) where numerical drift can cross threshold checks, and (2) scheduling-induced KV cache aliases when continuous batching mixes sequences with different policy hints. This PR implements a multi-pronged runtime mitigation: (A) fast-path gating that evaluates a cheap oracle before selecting an aggressive kernel, (B) per-request precision policy toggles with fallback coherence, and (C) a global 'safe-mode' that enforces conservative kernel selection for deployments that prioritize determinism over peak throughput. The changes are designed to be conservative by default and configurable per-deployment.

What this PR changes (high-level): - fast-path gating: a lightweight verification that runs at kernel-selection time; checks include sequence-length alignment, head-dim divisibility, kv-cache layout compatibility, and a floating-point stability heuristic. Gate returns ALLOW or DENY for fast kernels. When denied, runtime picks a conservative compatibility kernel. - precision toggles: requests may specify a preferred precision (fp32, bf16, int8) in the runtime flags. When an aggressive precision is selected, we attach a precision-stamp to the request and ensure that batched operations only group compatible stamps or demote to a conservative execution path. - safe-mode: a deployment/runtime flag that forces deterministic kernels (no fused/approximated kernels), disables some heuristics that risk nondeterminism (e.g. async kernel chaining), and enables stricter KV cache verification. Intended for regulated customers or incident mitigation. - KV cache invariants: added explicit verification hooks when moving KV shards between devices or reusing cached prefixes; these checks are lightweight by default but can be promoted to strict checks in safe-mode. - scheduling changes: continuous-batching scheduler now respects precision-stamps and fast-path gate outcomes when forming batches; the scheduler will split or reorder to preserve correctness rather than blindly maximizing batch size. - tests and benchmarks: added unit tests reproducing prior regression patterns and a micro-benchmark to measure fast-path gate overhead.

Description/notes for reviewers (single-line style): This is a behavioral change to kernel selection — default experience should be unchanged unless a customer enables precision overrides or safe-mode. The fast-path gate is intentionally cheap (single-digit microseconds for common inputs) and caches decisions per model/sequence-profile. The PR contains both the gate logic and the policy integration points (runtime flags, scheduler hooks). Please focus review on correctness of the KV cache invariants, scheduler batch-paths, and the interaction between precision-stamps and continuous batching.

Review conversation highlights: - Aarti: "Can you explain the gate cache invalidation strategy? I'm worried a long-lived cache could mask model upgrades." — Noah: "Gate caches are keyed by (model_id, model_checksum, profile_hash); we invalidate when model checksum changes. Added explicit invalidation in model-upgrade path (src/runtime/model_manager.cpp)." - Diego: "Scheduler change looks correct but we need to ensure we don't regress p50 latency for small requests." — Noah: "Bench numbers added; p50 unchanged, p95 improved by 4% in scenarios with mixed precision. Gate overhead is ~3us per decision and is amortized by cached results for common profiles." - Lena: "KV invariant verifier might be too expensive in strict mode; any way to sample?" — Noah: "Yes, we expose sample_rate and a strict boolean. Default strict=false; safe-mode forces strict=true. Documented in runtime-config.md." - Diego (post-approval): "Please add an opt-out flag for Dedicated customers who rely on the old aggressive kernel selection." — Noah: "Added --runtime-fastpath-opt-out and documented in Dedicated migration notes."

CI summary: - linux-build: pass - unit-tests: pass (one flaky test initially; re-run succeeded) - integration-tests: pass - bench-smoke: pass - lint: pass

Perf notes: - Continuous batching micro-bench shows fast-path gate adds 2-6% CPU overhead on tight loops but enables use of high-throughput kernels for 60% of steady workloads, resulting in net token/sec improvements of 8-12% on our RPU cluster for mixed-precision-enabled models. - In safe-mode, throughput is reduced (~18% on average) but p99 latency variance improves and numerical determinism is preserved.

Backward compatibility / migration: Default runtime behavior unchanged. New flags: --runtime-safe-mode (bool), --precision-preference (string), --runtime-fastpath-opt-out (bool). Dedicated/Private operators should review migration notes; safe-mode intended as an incident mitigation toggle.

Testing and validation: Added regression tests that reproduce previously observed KV aliasing read errors and precision-bound drift failures. Manual run against a staging fleet (redwood-staging) for 48h; no regressions observed. Bench harness included and results under tools/bench/README.md.

Follow-ups (future work): - Extend gate to consider dynamic temperature and response-length distributions - Add telemetry events for gate-deny reasons to improve ops diagnostics - Explore hardware-specific micro-optimizations for safe deterministic kernels
